03-violin-plot-orchestra.visual_critic_note: Intentional Tol Bright palette and typographic hierarchy show real design effort, but Singapore's row renders as near-invisible flat lines (looks broken, though technically correct), and the small cell size collapses the violin shapes into unreadable diamond glyphs that obscure the distributional detail the chart promises.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.encoding_integrity_note: Encoding is structurally honest — violin width uses correct linear-to-density mapping, domains are fully data-driven (d3.extent/d3.max), silverman bandwidth implemented correctly, and a shared y-scale across all cells enables honest cross-city comparison; minor deduction because KDE is extended 3×bandwidth beyond data extent while y-scale padding is fixed at ±5°C, risking tail clipping when bandwidth exceeds ~1.7°C.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.stress_test_note: No brush, zoom, or transitions present; pointer events unify mouse/touch cleanly, and pointermove only repositions the tooltip without triggering DOM mutations or re-renders.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.cognitive_load_note: 72 cells (6 cities × 12 months) is high but reads as a single conceptual matrix — the two-color split violin with shared y-scale lets seasonal arcs and decadal warming emerge as global patterns rather than forcing cell-by-cell comparison, and the restrained 2-hue palette eliminates color overload entirely.
